hero: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a polished FINAL TARGET LOOK concept image for SECOND WORKSHOP (二号车间) in a top-down prison factory game. This is a proposal image, not a screenshot of a finished implementation. Reference image 1 is the original master-plan crop defining the production-machine character; reference image 2 is the currently implemented first workshop and defines painting style and character scale. Match the supplied low-resolution original plan for machine arrangement and function, and the supplied existing workshop-one game screenshot for the art language: highly readable hand-painted 2D top-down orthographic game map, a modest visible front elevation on objects, perfectly straight horizontal and vertical map walls, no diamond isometric view, no dramatic perspective. Clean crisp dark painted outlines, restrained brush texture, upper-left soft light, muted slate blue machinery, desaturated olive-gray concrete / small industrial floor squares, warm gray plaster, charcoal gray lower wall dado and modest light concrete coping. Limited brass handwheels and warm wood storage accents. Restrained grime only near machine feet, no dense visual noise or blurry sand/grain, no photorealism, no 3D render look. Same consistent viewing angle and ground scale for every object. A wide rectangular workshop floor with width-to-depth ratio approximately 2:1, corresponding to 1460 by 720 game units. Four heavy machine stations in a 2-by-2 arrangement: top-left a long horizontal blue-gray metal lathe, bottom-left a second long lathe, bottom-right a medium horizontal precision lathe/milling bed, top-right a bulky vertical milling / motor drive machine on a cast-iron pedestal. These are industrial machines with integrated metal bases, NOT ordinary wooden desks carrying small motors. Each long machine occupies about 22-25 percent of interior width. A generous clear central north-south working aisle, and a clear cross aisle between rows. North doorway at 62 percent of room width, south doorway at 21 percent of width, east doorway at 67 percent of room depth. Aisle bends gently at north/south ends to meet these existing off-center doors; keep all three accessible. Continuous perimeter storage is broken at every doorway: low blue steel small-parts drawers and open cubby racks along north wall, narrow tall tool shelves and a stock-bar bin against west wall, electrical cabinet and small tool rack at east upper wall, short east supply shelves away from doorway, a few grouped wooden crates and two oil drums in unused corners. Leave a broad working apron in front of each machine and no storage down the central aisle. Present only this workshop building with its roof removed to reveal the finished interior, plus a narrow surrounding paved apron, no surrounding rooms, no editor UI, no red markup rectangles. Four large clearly different heavy machine stations are the focal point, their cast iron bases and handwheels readable; small yellow safety corner marks around their ground footprints, very subtle floor wear. Wall-mounted conduits and two small caged lights; gray-green industrial double steel doors, open at south entrance with two slim visible leaves; other doors also visually accessible. One small familiar orange-uniform chibi prisoner in central aisle for scale, head/body proportions matching screenshot; machine beds about three of this character's displayed heights long, never a giant character. A small physical ivory plaque reading exactly “二号车间” on front wall next to entrance. No floating room labels, no arrows, no explanatory text, no captions, no other words. Clean landscape composition, high resolution and detailed edges, entire workshop comfortably framed.
